verification_report.summary:
The supplied chapter passes sequential verification relative to the expressly accepted prerequisites. Every new deduction was checked in textual order. No critical errors or gaps were found. The class E_phi retains its convex-envelope definition and may contain infinite-mass potentials. No BMP, upper-volume bound, or raw mass equality is used. Positive v_-(theta) enters only in the domination section, and finiteness is assumed specifically for mu_u.

Stretch closure satisfies every defining parameter condition: t>bs makes both constructed expressions genuine convex combinations, yielding competitors for Q_b and then for every further stretch. Common translations preserve the ordered-pair argument. The difference envelope belongs to E_0 because semipositivity makes h_b/b admissible and hence h_b<=bw for every b>=1. All difference inequalities are interpreted off poles and then through canonical sums.

Finite rooftop closure is proved without circularity. Half-sums of P_theta(2b w_u) and P_theta(2b w_v) first establish the E_0 rooftop and all its scaling competitors. Adding the epsilon-background reference envelope to the appropriately scaled E_0 envelope supplies a genuine theta-background competitor. Only after pairwise nonemptiness is established is it applied to stretched pairs to prove relative class membership. Iteration handles finite collections.

For the smaller-background mass lemma, u-q is nonnegative and finite almost everywhere. Its envelope p in background (1-a)theta is bounded. Contact support, positive mixed products on finite levels, and ordered contact transfer the entire bounded measure of p to mu_u. Bounded measures charge none of the discarded pluripolar sets. Scaling p=(1-a)p_tilde gives the stated bound using the infimum over bounded theta-potentials. Bigness separately gives individual positive mass even when that infimum is zero. For every 0<delta<1-epsilon, the displayed competitor has exactly background (epsilon+delta)theta. Letting delta decrease to zero in the numerical estimates proves the uniform bound (1-epsilon)^n v_-(theta); no endpoint envelope or finiteness is asserted.

For domination, w=max(u,v) belongs to E_phi by upward stability, and locality preserves the strict-set measure inequality. Every q_b belongs to E_phi. On its contact set the pure mixed-product terms have coefficients b^(-n) and (1-1/b)^n. Restricting to {u,w,q_b>-k} makes all measures finite. Once (1-1/b)^n>c, cancellation forces both mu_w and mu_{q_b} to vanish on the strict contact part. Exhaustion is legitimate because the measures vanish on pluripolar sets. Remaining mass lies where q_b=u. Ordered contact for q_b<=u therefore gives mu_{q_b}<=1_{q_b=u}mu_u with coefficient exactly ONE, independent of b.

The envelopes decrease along integers. Collapse would force M_b=sup_X q_b to decrease to minus infinity and imply kappa<=mu_u({u<=M_b})→0. This limit uses the finite measure mu_u and its zero mass on {u=-infinity}; finiteness of only mu_v does not justify this step. Thus the limit q is genuine. The obstacle inequality forces each finite strict set {u<w-a} into its pole set. Countable choices of b and a give equality almost everywhere, and canonical representatives give equality everywhere, including at poles. No class membership or measure convergence for the limiting q is needed.

Exponential order follows by cancelling finite positive weights off poles and applying domination to v-a. Constant translations prove the scalar-ratio assertion. For an exponential equation with finite reference measure, boundedness above of each solution makes its Monge-Ampere measure finite, permitting comparison in both directions. Positive scalar uniqueness follows by comparing both ratios. The proof correctly makes no zero-exponent uniqueness-modulo-constants claim.

The required theorem searches were followed by web fallback and primary-source inspection. The attributions match Propositions 3.5–3.8 and the finite-mu_u specialization of Theorem 3.14 in [ALS26 v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.02339v1). Its definitions agree with the chapter's envelope class, smaller-background model condition, and possibly infinite measures. The source's broader alternative allowing either measure to be finite was not imported. All conclusions here were checked independently from the accepted prerequisites.
